cards.text: Saul and his son Jonathan are dead, and David has poured out his grief for them in a song (2 Samuel 1:17-27). Some time later, David doesn't just pack up and make a move. He asks the LORD first: should he go up to one of the towns of Judah?

cards.question: When David asks about going up to a town of Judah, the LORD tells him to wait.
David asks a follow-up question: where should he go? The LORD answers: go to ___.

cards.text: Two questions, two answers, and David heads up to Hebron, but not alone. Baker, I have spent LONGER than that deciding between sprinkles and chocolate chips.

cards.question: Who goes with David to Hebron?

answers.text: His two wives Ahinoam and Abigail
His father Jesse and his brothers
The prophet Samuel and the priests

cards.text: David's men come along too, every one of them with his whole household. That's not moving day, friend, that's a PARADE, and they all settle in the towns near Hebron.

cards.question: Then the men of Judah come to David in Hebron. What do they do there?

answers.text: Anoint him king over the house of Judah
Ask him to lead them against the Philistines
Hand him the crown from Saul's head

cards.question: In Hebron, the men of Judah anoint David king over every tribe of Israel.

cards.text: Then the men of Judah pass along some news. Saul fell in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:1-6), and someone gave him a burial.

cards.question: The men of Judah tell David that the men of ___ buried Saul.

cards.text: So David sends messengers to Jabesh-gilead, even though Saul spent day after day hunting him (1 Samuel 23:14). Friend, if somebody chased ME around for years, I'd need a WHOLE batch of cookies just to calm my mustache down enough to hold a pencil.

cards.question: What message does David send to the men of Jabesh-gilead?

answers.text: The LORD bless you for your kindness to Saul
The LORD guard you as you mourn for Saul
The LORD reward you for joining my army

cards.question: David's message tells the men of Jabesh-gilead may the LORD show them loving devotion, and David promises to show them favor too because of what they did.
David tells the men of Jabesh-gilead to be strong and courageous. What reason does he give them?

answers.text: Saul is dead but Judah has anointed David king
The Philistines are marching toward their town
The LORD has promised them a great victory

cards.text: Meanwhile, Saul's side is NOT just sitting around. Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, is about to make a big move.

cards.question: Abner, the commander of Saul's army, takes someone and moves him to Mahanaim. Who is it?
Abner makes Ish-bosheth king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin. That's king over all ___.
Ish-bosheth is forty years old when he begins to reign over Israel, and he reigns for two years.
The house of Judah sticks with David. How long is David king in Hebron over the house of Judah?

cards.text: Hold on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: "So David sends messengers to Jabesh-gilead, even though Saul spent day after day hunting him" ties David's message to Saul's pursuit. That presents the message as graciousness toward an enemy, but 2 Samuel 2:5 never makes that connection. The joke also says "for years", which adds a time the cited text (1 Samuel 23:14, "day after day") doesn't give.

rule.text: **Connecting passages.** When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: "for years" in the joke implies a length of time for Saul's pursuit that 1 Samuel 23:14 doesn't state.

rule.text: **Times stay true.** No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The core action of the moment is David sending a blessing and kindness to Saul's loyal men. The joke's action is being rattled after being chased and needing cookies to calm down. That is a different action, so the comparison doesn't match the fact.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Saul's armor-bearer" is a different kind of answer from the other two. It is shorter and has no name, while the others follow the pattern "[someone]'s son [name]". That makes the right answer and Mephibosheth stand together, and the armor-bearer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason about Ish-bosheth's age at the start of his reign or how long he reigned. The only way to get this true or false right is luck, and no story card gives context first.

rule.text: **The check:** could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: "Two years" is much shorter than "Seven years and six months" and "Three years and six months", so it stands apart from the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the "this story is NOT done" line and tells no verse, but it cites 2 Samuel 2:11. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none. The JSON shape still requires a verses value.
findings.question: What should the "verses" field be on a closing story card that is only the story-continues line and tells no verse: the passage's last verse, null, or something else?
